newsitem.title: CANADA: Manitoba harvest slowed by rain, good yield, grade.
newsitem.headline: Manitoba harvest slowed by rain, good yield, grade.

text.p: Severe thundershowers last Wednesday and Thursday delayed harvest progress and damaged a few fields, Manitoba Agriculture's report for the week ended September 9 said.
Southwest Manitoba - Fifty percent of cereals were harvested with yields seen at or above average. Eighty percent of wheat graded number one, the rest was number two and three.

Northwest Manitoba - Eighty percent of canola and 60 percent of wheat were swathed. Fifty percent of harvested wheat graded number one with yields averaging at 35 bushels an acre, canola yielded 25 to 30 bu/ac.

Central Manitoba - More than 50 percent of cereals and 25 percent of canola was combined in the southwest. Wheat yields ranged 35 to 45 bu/ac with most grading number two. Canola yielded 35 to 40 bu/ac.
Districts just west of Winnipeg combined 50 percent of wheat and 10 percent of canola. Most wheat graded number one. Wheat yields ranged 35 to 50 bu/ac.

Eastern Manitoba - Harvest progressed rapidly. Dominion City and Steinbach reported 75 percent of wheat and barley combined with the rest of the region at 50 percent. Canola was 70 to 90 percent swathed.
Yields in canola were 30 bu/ac, wheat was 40 bu/ac, barley was 70 to 80 bu/ac and oats were 80 to 100 bu/ac. Grades ranged from number one to three.

Interlake region - Seventy-five percent of wheat, barley was swathed and 35 percent was combined. Canola was 85 percent swathed and five percent combined. Oats were 60 percent swathed, 25 percent combined. Yields were above average with good quality, 80 percent of wheat graded number one.
